Projects.title: Selected work
Projects.subtitle: A few projects I'm proud of — real clients, real problems, shipped.

cocky.title: Cocky Scooters
cocky.description: A scooter rental business in Tivat needed a complete digital presence before tourist season. I handled design, development, and print materials end-to-end.
cocky.problem: No website, no brand identity, and a tight deadline before peak season.
cocky.result: Launched a trilingual site with custom branding, blog, and print flyers — ready for the season.

fashion.title: Fashion White
fashion.description: A full e-commerce platform with product catalog, cart, and checkout. Along the way, I tracked down a Supabase security bug that was silently killing all mobile orders.
fashion.problem: Mobile customers were completing checkout, but orders never reached the database.
fashion.result: Found and fixed a Row Level Security misconfiguration. Orders now work reliably across all devices.

ai_agents.title: Multi-Agent AI System
ai_agents.description: An orchestration system where three specialized AI agents — Planner, Researcher, and Writer — collaborate to produce content autonomously.
ai_agents.problem: Single-prompt AI workflows hit a wall when tasks get complex.
ai_agents.result: A working pipeline that breaks down tasks, researches, and writes — built on FastAPI and React.

cocky.overview: Cocky Scooters is a scooter rental business in Tivat, Montenegro. Before the tourist season, they needed a full digital presence — not just a website, but a complete brand.
cocky.solution: I built a trilingual site (English, Montenegrin, Russian) with a blog for SEO, a custom design system, and a visual rebrand. On top of that, I designed and produced print flyers and physical stickers using Python and Pillow for image processing.
cocky.long_result: The client got a fast, professional site ready for peak season — with a complete brand identity, print materials, and a content system they can manage themselves. No ongoing developer dependency.

fashion.overview: Fashion White is an online clothing store. The goal was a complete shopping experience — from browsing to checkout — built to be fast and reliable.
fashion.solution: I built the whole thing with React, Vite, and Supabase: product catalog with filters, cart, secure checkout, and order management. During testing, I noticed mobile orders were silently failing. After digging through Supabase logs, I traced it to a Row Level Security policy that was blocking anonymous mobile sessions.
fashion.long_result: Fixed the RLS policy and shipped a fully working store. The debugging alone prevented what would have been a significant loss of mobile sales — and taught me a lot about Supabase security.

ai_agents.overview: A demonstration of how specialized AI agents can collaborate to produce better output than any single model call. Built as a portfolio piece targeting AI engineering roles.
ai_agents.solution: Three agents — Planner, Researcher, Writer — each with a focused responsibility, communicating through a structured pipeline. Planner decomposes the task, Researcher gathers context, Writer produces the final output. FastAPI backend, React and Vite frontend, deployed on Render and Vercel.
ai_agents.long_result: A working demo showing how multi-agent systems handle complex tasks that single prompts can't. The architecture is the real output — clean separation of concerns, clear data flow between agents, and a UI that makes the process visible.

About.title: Hospitality first, then code.
About.p1: Before I wrote my first line of code, I spent several years working in hospitality. It's not the background most developers have, but it taught me how to read people, stay calm when things get stressful, and actually deliver — not just promise. Those habits carried over more than I expected.
About.p2: I learned development the long way — documentation, side projects, a lot of trial and error. No shortcut, no single mentor, just consistent work over time. I still approach new tools the same way: start with the docs, build something small, then something real.
About.p3: These days I'm based in Tivat, building web applications for clients and open to joining a team full-time. I try to keep it simple: understand the problem, write code I'd be happy to inherit, and ship something that actually works.
